correctness.rationale: The full symmetric group acts orthogonally and transitively on edge coordinates, and averaging orbit centers preserves containment of a Euclidean ball, so an optimal incenter may be taken constant. The inspected irredundant facet theorem gives all relevant facet orbits. Their exact distances from a constant point are computed and balanced against coordinate-facet distance. The odd-set balance denominator increases with odd-set size, so only the largest odd set can compete; direct comparison yields the exceptional sizes 3, 5, and 7 and the tie at 4. Uniqueness follows because all center coordinates are at least the radius while an active shrunken degree or global odd-set facet forces their relevant sum to equal the sum of these lower bounds. For the circumradius, distance from a constant center depends only on matching cardinality; exact quadratic minimization gives the stated center and radius, and strong convexity gives uniqueness. The finite checker only corroborates the arbitrary-n proof.

value.rationale: The result determines both fundamental Euclidean ball radii, both optimal centers, and the exact contact sets for a classical high-dimensional polytope family. The inradius exhibits a nontrivial facet-orbit phase: blossom facets dominate only in dimensions corresponding to n=3,5,7, tie with degree facets at n=4, and degree facets dominate thereafter. The circumradius identifies maximum matchings as exactly the outer contact vertices. These are structural metric statements across all n, not isolated computations or a simple renaming of the facet theorem.
